text:
For a rental, I’d start with the **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W solar panel kit**. It’s a portable battery-and-panel setup: put the panel out on the balcony to charge the battery, then bring the panel in when needed. The 288 Wh battery should suit phones, a laptop, a router, or a fan—but **not** a fridge or heater. [Kit details and buy link](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-an-apartment-balcony)

If you want more backup capacity, the **Anker SOLIX C800X** is a larger 960 Wh option described as a pick for balcony solar recharging; check whether you’re buying the panel separately. [Apartment power-station guide](https://powerbencher.com/stories/home-backup/best-portable-power-stations-apartment/)

These are battery power stations, not systems that connect to your apartment’s wiring. Before setting up a panel, check your lease/building rules and make sure it can be secured safely without drilling.
